questions.q: In what ratio does the x-axis divide the segment joining A(-4,-6) and B(-1,7), and what is the point of division?
questions.explanation: Let the x-axis point P divide AB internally in the ratio m:n = AP:PB. Using the y-coordinate, (7m - 6n)/(m+n) = 0, so 7m = 6n and m:n = 6:7. The x-coordinate is [6(-1)+7(-4)]/13 = -34/13, giving P(-34/13,0).

questions.q: Point A(2,-4) is equidistant from P(3,8) and Q(-10,y). What are the possible values of y?
The segment joining A(3,2) and B(5,1) is divided internally at P in the ratio 1:2. If P lies on 3x - 18y + k = 0, find k.
questions.explanation: For AP:PB = 1:2, the section formula gives P = ((1x5+2x3)/3, (1x1+2x2)/3) = (11/3, 5/3). Substituting into 3x - 18y + k = 0 gives 11 - 30 + k = 0. Therefore k = 19.

questions.q: A(-2,3), B(6,7) and C(8,3) are consecutive vertices of parallelogram ABCD. What is D?
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so A + C = B + D coordinate-wise. Therefore D = A + C - B. This gives D = (-2+8-6, 3+3-7) = (0,-1).
